polymorphic.discriminator: (num_nonnulls(candidate_id, claim_id, claim_conflict_id, entity_merge_id, operation_intent_id, capability_version_id, vector_space_version_id) = 1)
(num_nonnulls(entity_id, record_id, chunk_id, claim_id, summary_id, document_node_id, digest_id, authored_revision_id, passage_id) = 1)

domains.body:
`access.account_profile` (`set_account_profile`) holds age band and preferences;
`access.guardian_link` (`invite_guardian`, `consent_guardian`) and
`access.processing_authorization` (`authorize_processing`) record consent, checked by
`product.processing_allowed`. `access.client_grant` (`create_client_grant`,
`revoke_client_grant`) lets an MCP server or CLI act for a principal within a scope
(author, learn, library, assess, read); `product.client_grant` resolves the caller and
decides whether the actor is human (web or interactive CLI) or an agent.
`access.policy_version` (`add_policy_version`) is the workspace grading/finalization policy
read by `product.policy`; `access.provided_credential` (`issue_provided_credential`) and
`access.source_restriction` (`restrict_source`) are worker-managed.

Agents reach these only through operations; there are no reader views. Trap: a client
grant can never mint grants (`FORBIDDEN`), and agent-kind actors cannot record human
reviews or finalize results that the policy reserves for humans.
domains.summary: Who may act (lens ours): account profiles, MCP/CLI client grants, guardian consent, processing authorizations, policy versions, source restrictions.
domains.title: Access (accounts, grants, policies, consent)

domains.body:
`acquisition.fetch` is one attempt to obtain bytes from a URL: who (origin_kind,
origin_label, actor or Mission Control run), with what tool and version, when, HTTP status,
outcome, content hash, media type, size, credits and USD spent, failure class. It exists so
spend and honesty are visible before any document is created. When bytes are kept, the
capture row (`evidence.source_capture.acquisition_fetch_id`) points back at the fetch.

`outcome = unchanged` means the same bytes as `prior_capture_id`: no new
`content.document_version` is created and `content.refresh_check` records `unchanged` for
the document. `changed` creates a version and a refresh_check with `new_version_id`; the
unit grammar then diffs the two versions by logical key into `content.unit_change`, which
`api.changes_since` reports beside fact changes and which drives update proposals for facts.

Read `q:acquisition.fetches_for_url` for a URL's history and spend,
`q:content.refresh_checks` for a document's refresh outcomes, `q:content.unit_changes` for
what moved. Search/provider attempts (`evidence.source_query`, `evidence.provider_result`)
stay in `evidence` for now. Writers are `executor_service`; harness fetches are recorded by
the product worker, never by agents directly.
domains.summary: Every fetch is a ledger row before it becomes a capture; refreshes record unchanged/changed/failed even when nothing moved.
domains.title: Acquisition and refresh

domains.body:
`api` has no tables. **L1 catalog views** (lens corpus unless noted) answer filter / compare /
rank questions with no embeddings: `api.models` (one row per model version with developer,
release date, context, modalities, capability statuses, cutoff, availability and the minimum
current price per 1M tokens), `api.model_offerings` (model as sold by a provider, normalized
USD per 1M tokens for input/output/cached/batch, with the exact claim and locator behind the
input price), `api.software` (+ the `api.libraries`, `api.repositories`, `api.mcp_servers`,
`api.agent_skills` slices), `api.software_releases`, `api.talks`, `api.people`,
`api.organizations`, `api.events`, `api.concepts`, `api.papers`, `api.benchmark_scores`,
`api.guidance_items`, and `api.works_authored` (lens ours, tier 1: our courses, modules,
reports at head). Every L1 row carries `as_of_knowledge_seq` or `learned_k` so you can cite
the head.

**L2 facts and time**: `api.changes_since(since, stream_kinds, entity_kinds, document_types)`,
`api.price_history(offering, meter)`, `api.fact_locators(entity, stream_kind, scope_key)`,
`api.entity_at`, `api.what_changed`, `api.models_at` / `api.model_offerings_at` (L1 replayed
at a world time), `api.modules_affected_by_release(release)`.

**L3 scoped semantic**: `api.search_unified` (facets: lens, tier, space, document type, unit
kind, entity, as-of, workspace), `api.talk_segments(talk, from_ms, to_ms, query)`,
`api.document_units(document, unit_kinds)`, `api.document_digest(document)`.

**Product**: `api.product_command(workspace, operation, idempotency_key, expected_head,
payload)`, `api.product_read(workspace, operation, payload)` for `authenticated`;
`api.product_worker(operation, payload)` for `service_role`. The operations are one page
each under `ops/` (see INDEX.md).

Older surface: `api.entities`, `api.current_facts` (applies `k_to is null` and
`valid_during @> now()` — the usual trap; historical reads use `api.entity_at`),
`api.current_relationships`, `api.events_current`, `api.hybrid_knowledge_search_1536`.
`util.current_tenant_id` reads the app.tenant_id GUC and fails closed; every call needs it.
Invariant: `app_reader` never SELECTs catalog or temporal tables. Long-tail reads are new
catalog entries, not raw SQL.
domains.summary: The only surface apps and agents see; invoker views and definer RPCs organised as the L1–L3 knowledge continuum.
domains.title: API surface (L1 views, L2 and L3 functions)

domains.body:
`authoring.workspace` is a personal or shared team container with `authoring.workspace_member`
roles (owner, editor, reader). `authoring.work` is the identity of a course, module, lesson,
activity, brief, report, template or dataset; `authoring.work_revision` is immutable and
`work.head_revision_id` is the mutable pointer (`revise_work` requires `p_expected_head`).
Bodies are typed blocks (`authoring.revision_block`, `authoring.block_type`);
`authoring.revision_binding` records which catalog entities, software or software versions a
revision uses or covers, and `authoring.runtime_requirement` what it needs to run — this is
what `api.works_authored.covers_concepts/uses_software` and
`api.modules_affected_by_release` read.

Every state change is an `authoring.event` (actor kind human/agent, surface web/harness,
review decisions with `closure_sha256`) and every command an `authoring.command` row keyed
by idempotency key and input digest. Release: `freeze_release` computes the exposure of a
root revision (`product.exposure`), applies author decisions to blockers and freezes
`authoring.release` + `authoring.release_item`; `open_distribution` / `offer_release` publish
it through `authoring.distribution` and `authoring.distribution_offer` to members or the
public library; `authoring.publisher_grant` gates official publication. Assets
(`authoring.asset_scope`, `authoring.file_set`, `authoring.deployment`) register uploaded
artifacts, file sets and deployed static sites.

Read our works with `q:ours.works_authored`; write only through operations
(`ops/create_work.md`, `ops/revise_work.md`, `ops/review_revision.md`,
`ops/freeze_release.md`, `ops/offer_release.md`). Released course material is indexed with
lens ours, tier 1, in the `own_content` space. Trap: agents may propose but not record human
reviews (release_review, official_publication).
domains.summary: What we author (lens ours): immutable revisions of courses, modules, lessons, activities, briefs, reports and datasets; releases freeze closures for distribution.
domains.title: Authoring (works, revisions, releases, distribution)

domains.body:
`content.document` is the identity of a captured work (`work_entity_id` for talks, papers
and other work entities; `source_role_code` says who speaks: first_party, filer, academic,
registry, third_party_editorial, community, own, system). Kinds are open-world:
`content.document_type` rows can be `candidate` until their grammar settles, assignments
are append-only in `content.document_kind_assignment` (current one has
`superseded_by_id` null), and `unclassified` is always valid. Versions carry the
`format_code` axis (`content.format`: html, pdf, markdown, timed_text, slides, json, …) that
decides parser and locator kinds; representations carry the `grammar_version` that produced
their units.

Before a kind or grammar is assigned, `content.structure_census` records what a
representation structurally contains (headings, tables, lists, code, timecodes, speakers,
figures). The grammar is data: `content.unit_kind` lists the typed units a document kind
decomposes into (price_row, transcript_segment, slide, release_entry, table_row, section,
code_block, …) with a JSON Schema for attributes, the `logical_key_attributes` that make a
unit stable across captures, the selector kind and the retrieval role. `content.document_node`
is the typed unit: `unit_kind` (+version), validated `attributes`, `logical_key`, and typed
position (offsets, page, bbox, `start_ms`/`end_ms`). `content.unit_entity_role` says which
entity a unit is about and in what role; `content.unit_assertion_mapping` says how a unit
kind's attributes become an assertion.

Read units with `q:content.document_units`, a talk's transcript window with
`q:content.talk_segments`, and the structured digest with `q:content.document_digest`:
`content.document_digest` items are records anchored to unit node ids (key points, entity
roles, assertion references, changes, open questions, research directions); prose summaries
(`content.document_summary.digest_id`) render a digest and are never evidence.
`api.summary_evidence` expands a summary into faithful nodes and locators.

Refresh is data: `content.refresh_check` records unchanged/changed/failed per document and
`content.unit_change` the unit-level diff between two versions matched by logical key.
Agents read structure to compose locators and packets; they do not rewrite faithful content
or write units. Trap: treating a transcript segment as a fact — the world interval still
lives on a `temporal.segment`; the unit only locates the quote.
domains.summary: Faithful documents decomposed into typed units with stable logical keys; census before kind, digests anchored to units, refresh as data.
domains.title: Documents, typed units, census and digests

domains.body:
Courses, modules and activities are authored works in the `authoring` schema; every
curriculum row hangs off an `authoring.work_revision`. `curriculum.part` places a child
revision inside a parent revision at an ordinal, as `recommended` or `optional`.
`curriculum.outcome` states what a learner can do after a revision (optional Bloom level,
an `aieng.evidence-rule` for proof). `curriculum.requirement` is what completion needs: an
`outcome` or a `mandatory_activity` (a part). `curriculum.requirement_option` lists the
routes that satisfy it (`standard`, `prior_work`, `test_out`, `alternative`,
`generated_eligible`, `learner_project`), each `proposed` until approved.
`curriculum.prerequisite` links revisions as `recommended` or `required`.
`curriculum.outcome_alignment` maps an outcome to a competency revision by facet.

Releases change over time: `curriculum.release_transition` maps one `authoring.release`
to the next (`needs_review`, `compatible`, `breaking`), and
`curriculum.requirement_transition` says per requirement whether learner progress carries,
needs reassessment or does not apply.

These rows are written by product operations (create_work, revise_work, freeze_release),
never directly. Invariants: rows reference revisions, never mutable heads; a part cannot
contain itself; a requirement is exactly one kind. Trap: putting a product availability
date in course structure; that fact belongs on
`temporal.stream_kind:model_offering_availability`, cited from content.
domains.summary: Structure, outcomes and requirements of authored course works, keyed to authoring revisions (machinery lens: written by product operations).
domains.title: Curriculum structure

domains.body:
Evaluation owns datasets, cases, graders, runs, scores, review tasks, experiments,
promotion gates, and verification benchmark ledgers. `api.review_queue` exposes
`evaluation.review_task`. Review tasks may point at a staging candidate, an entity merge,
a claim conflict or a vector-space version.

This domain measures systems; it does not store industry facts. A grader score is not a
`temporal.segment`; a model's benchmark result is a `benchmark_score` stream fact shown in
`api.benchmark_scores`. Verification benchmark runs compare sealed verification arms and are
distinct from the component's own verification runs. Gate results decide promotion of a
system, not publication of a fact.

Trap: using `evaluation.metric_observation` as if it were a fact stream. When identity is
uncertain, `stage-uncertain-candidate` plus `q:staging.unresolved` is the agent path;
evaluation may later attach a `evaluation.review_task` to that candidate.
domains.summary: Datasets, graders, review tasks, and verification benchmarks (machinery lens).
domains.title: Evaluation

domains.body:
Lineage is `evidence.source` → `evidence.source_capture` (artifact_id, content_sha256,
capture_method, and since Build 08 `acquisition_fetch_id` when a product/harness fetch
produced the bytes) → `evidence.locator` (selector, selected_content_sha256, normalized
value, timecode or page) → `evidence.claim`. `evidence.claim_subject` names entities as
subject, object, or context. Canonical facts attach a `primary_claim_id` and, separately,
k-stamped `evidence.segment_support` rows that point at a segment or an event occurrence
plus a locator. `q:facts.locators` (`api.fact_locators`) walks a current fact back to its
claim, locator, capture URL/time and the typed unit (`content.document_node`) it was read
from — the answer to "where did this number come from".

Act 2 and act 3: `evidence.extraction_record` anchors a faithful extraction on a typed unit
(`document_node_id`) and names the `content.unit_assertion_mapping` that interpreted it.
Discovery leads are `evidence.source_query` → `evidence.provider_result` →
`evidence.source_encounter`. Capture methods and search providers are vocabularies.

Acts 4–5 live in the shared Knowledge Services engine; this database keeps the admission
ledger. A claim reaches `verified` only under a receipt bound to an admitted use decision,
with `verification.use_admission` written by `verification.assert_admitted_use` in the same
transaction (ADMISSION_REQUIRED otherwise). `verification.use_admission` is append-only.

app_reader cannot see evidence tables directly; it reaches them through `api.fact_locators`,
`api.model_offerings.price_claim_id/price_locator_id` and `api.benchmark_scores.claim_id`.
Use `q:evidence.claims_for_entity` and `q:evidence.claim_support` as pipeline_agent.
Inserts into source/capture/locator/claim are permitted to pipeline_agent and
executor_service; `evidence.segment_support` is helper-only (`temporal.admit_support`).

Traps: do not treat a verification run as already in `evidence.claim` — materialize cited
claims first. Support role is supports, challenges or context. A prose summary is not
evidence; only a locator on a captured unit is.
domains.summary: Source to capture to locator to claim; facts attach through segment_support; verified use is admitted in verification.use_admission.
domains.title: Source, evidence and admission

domains.body:
`guidance.item` (formerly knowledge.record) is one expert knowledge statement: `kind` from
`guidance.item_kind` (technical_problem, solution_pattern, failure_mode,
compatibility_constraint, operational_practice, implementation_example,
security_consideration, advanced_usage_pattern, setup_guide_step, research_direction),
title, statement, `scope`, `assurance_level` (`guidance.assurance_level`), a provenance
claim, `applies_to_version_ids` and a typed `payload` validated by the kind's
`payload_schema`. `guidance.item_subject` names the entities it is about and their role
(subject, component, version, alternative). `source_node_id` anchors it on the typed unit
it was learned from.

Read with `q:guidance.items` (`api.guidance_items`, lens corpus, filter by kind, entity or
text) or through `api.concepts.guidance_items` counts. Items are also retrieval projection
targets (`retrieval.projection_target.record_id`) and evidence-packet members, so
`q:retrieval.search_unified` finds them by text.

Only `executor_service` creates items, and `created_by_receipt_id` is required. These are
not temporal segments: a price or availability fact belongs in `temporal.segment`; a
how-to-call-the-API pattern belongs here, linked to the library entity and backed by a
claim. Course content cites these rows rather than restating them. Trap: writing a
benchmark number here when it is a `benchmark_score` stream fact.
domains.summary: Typed expert knowledge items (problem, pattern, failure mode, constraint, practice, example, security, usage) bound to entities, created only with a receipt.
domains.title: Expert guidance items

domains.body:
`catalog.entity` is the identity. `kind` is a foreign key to `taxonomy.entity_kind`
(36 kinds: organization, person, ai_model, ai_model_version, model_offering, library,
repository, mcp_server, agent_skill, paper, talk, concept, technique, …). Since Build 08
the thirty-six thin typed tables are gone: kind-specific attributes live in
`catalog.entity.attributes` and trigger `catalog.validate_entity_attributes` checks them
against `taxonomy.entity_kind.attributes_schema` (pg_jsonschema). Numbers that change over
time (prices, context windows, headcount, stars) are fact streams in `temporal`, never
attributes. `parent_kind` says which kind a kind versions (model version → model); the link
itself is a `catalog.relationship`. Work kinds (`is_work`: paper, talk, media_work, story,
case_study) also have a bibliographic row in `catalog.work`; their content is
`content.document` rows with `work_entity_id`.

Resolve before creating. `q:entity.resolve` (`api.resolve_entity`) matches display name,
alias and identifier value and returns at most 25 active rows. Prefer
`q:entity.by_identifier` when the source prints a schemed id: `(scheme, value)` is unique
per tenant. `q:entity.attributes` returns the row with its attributes and the kind's schema.
`q:entity.card` is the current overview for agents on `app_reader`. For a table of a kind
(all models, all organizations) go to the L1 views in `dom:api-surface` instead.

Aliases are typed (synonym, acronym, former_name, handle, ticker, slug, misspelling,
translation, model_alias) and unique per entity, not globally. Identifiers use a closed
`scheme` check; unknown namespaces belong in `other`. Merges are `catalog.entity_merge`
rows: the loser becomes `lifecycle='merged'` with `merged_into_id`; resolve excludes them.

Writers are `executor_service` only, and every entity needs `created_by_receipt_id`.
Agents author entity.create / entity.alias / entity.identifier proposals with an
`attributes` object; if resolve is ambiguous use candidate.stage. Traps: treating
display_name as a unique key; inventing identifier schemes; putting a price or a date
that moves into attributes; creating a `model_offering` without its parent
`ai_model_version` (the `offered_as` relationship and `parent_kind`).
domains.summary: One canonical row per industry identity; kind-specific attributes are a validated jsonb, not typed tables.
domains.title: Identities (catalog)

domains.body:
A research request starts as a `brief` work whose revision metadata is validated by
`product.proposal_problems` (`propose_research`). `inquiry.acceptance` records that a
workspace accepted it with numbered `inquiry.obligation` rows; `inquiry.delivery`
(`deliver_output`, `decide_delivery`) ties an output revision — usually a `report` work —
to an obligation. `inquiry.assertion` is a statement inside a report revision and
`inquiry.support` its typed support (source revision, locator, capture, claim, guidance
item, assertion, dataset cell or decision; `add_support`, `get_support`, `trace_assertion`,
`trace_reverse`). `inquiry.watch` (`create_watch`, `set_watch_state`) keeps a question open
for refresh.

Datasets are works too: `dataset.field` defines columns, `dataset.row` and `dataset.cell`
hold revisioned values (a version is visible in revision n when from <= n < to), and
`dataset.proposal` carries proposed changes (`propose_dataset_change`,
`decide_dataset_change`). `commit_dataset_revision` snapshots cells into an immutable work
revision (`product.dataset_snapshot`).

This is where L4 answers land: a research loop files its result as a report revision and
supports each assertion with `q:facts.locators` locators or claims rather than prose.
Operation pages: `ops/propose_research.md`, `ops/deliver_output.md`, `ops/add_support.md`,
`ops/get_report.md`, `ops/create_dataset.md`. Trap: support by prose summary; only a
locator, claim, cell or decision counts.
domains.summary: Build 07 research loop (lens ours): a brief is accepted with obligations, outputs are delivered, assertions carry typed support, datasets are revisioned cells.
domains.title: Inquiry and datasets (research requests, assertions, support)

domains.body:
`knowledge_service.operation` is the durable record of a platform or eve call
(operation_kind, idempotency_key, ownership_mode standalone | mission_control | eve,
attempt_id, request_sha256, status). Steps and events decompose the run. The outbox
emits knowledge.batch_sealed when a temporal batch commits and projection.rebuilt
when retrieval projections refresh.

Leases, callback deliveries, and eve operation bindings are runtime control. Agents
do not write these tables. The knowledge executor records a `knowledge_ingestion`
operation when it applies an intent. If a batch sealed but an artifact upload is pending,
the artifact row keeps `storage_state='pending'` and a retry step finishes it.

Trap: treating the outbox as a query catalog — agents should `check-knowledge-head` /
`q:knowledge.head` after a sealed batch instead of polling `knowledge_service.outbox`.
`temporal.emit_outbox` runs inside `temporal.commit_batch`; do not call it yourself.
domains.summary: Durable KS operations, steps, outbox, and eve bindings (machinery lens).
domains.title: Knowledge service runtime

domains.body:
`learning.enrollment` ties a learner to a `authoring.distribution_offer`;
`learning.release_adoption` records which frozen release they follow (`adopt_release`).
`learning.attempt` → `learning.submission` → `learning.evidence_item` (revision, artifact,
message, file set, deployment or external reference, hashed) is the proof trail;
`learning.evidence_grant` lets a learner share evidence with a reviewer.
`learning.grading_run` and `learning.criterion_result` are the worker's grading
(`record_grading`); `learning.assessment_result` is finalized by `product.finalize` under
the workspace policy (`access.policy_version`) either automatically or after human review
(`finalize_result`). `learning.mastery_decision`, `learning.appeal` (`open_appeal`,
`resolve_appeal`), `learning.credit` and `learning.equivalence_request`
(`propose_equivalence`, `decide_equivalence`) complete the loop;
`learning.environment_session` (`request_environment`) provisions a harness or browser
runtime.

Read progress through the `progress` and `get_result` operations (`ops/progress.md`,
`ops/get_result.md`); there are no app_reader views over learning rows. Private learner
notes are not here: they are `library.passage` rows with lens private. Trap: an agent
acting through a harness grant may propose but not record human review outcomes.
domains.summary: What learners do (lens ours): enroll in an offer, adopt a release, attempt activities, submit evidence, get graded, appeal, earn credit.
domains.title: Learning (enrollment, attempts, assessment)

domains.body:
Build 08 dropped the `public.research_*` and `public.factory_*` tables and the `research`,
`provenance` and `research_private` schemas. What remains in `public` is two trigger
helpers (`public.set_updated_at`, `public.reject_immutable_row_change`) used by older
tables. Nothing here is a navigation target; it is listed so INDEX.md stays complete.
domains.summary: The public schema holds no tables since Build 08; two generic trigger functions remain.
domains.title: Legacy (public schema)

domains.body:
`library.connection` + `library.connected_item` bring outside resources (uploads, repos,
documents) into a workspace; `library.preparation` records how an item was prepared and
`library.passage` is the indexed text unit (a revision, an uploaded artifact or a
conversation message, with locator, text and tsvector). `library.removal` (two-step:
`preview_removal`, `confirm_removal`) and `library.resource_control` (`set_control`) govern
exclusion and deletion; retiring passages also retires their vector items
(`retrieval.retire_items_for_passages`).

`conversation.thread` and `conversation.message` are the learner's or author's dialogue
(`create_thread`, `append_message`), with `conversation.context_snapshot` /
`conversation.context_item` recording what context a turn saw. Messages become passages too.

Everything here is lens `private`, RLS-isolated per workspace; the worker `index_passages`
indexes them into the `learner_notes` space (or `own_content` with lens ours once a work is
released). The product `search` operation (`ops/search.md`) calls `api.search_unified` with
lenses private+ours and the caller's workspace ids, then applies the readability rules
(member of the workspace, readable revision, shared asset, own or workspace-visible thread).
Trap: calling `q:retrieval.search_unified` with lens private and no `workspace_ids` returns
nothing — private items are returned only for the workspaces passed in.
domains.summary: A workspace's own material — uploaded sources, notes, conversations — as passages indexed with lens private (or ours when released).
domains.title: Library and conversation (private lens)

domains.body:
Observability stores traces, spans, raw and normalized events, usage rollups, IO
links, and coordinator handoffs. Event and span tables are month-partitioned.
This is runtime telemetry for missions and executors, not industry knowledge.

Agents debugging a failed ingest should look here only after the receipt and
knowledge head. Do not copy span attributes into `temporal.segment`. Normalized
events are the query surface; raw events are the append-only capture.
`observability.usage_rollup` aggregates tokens and cost for experiment metrics;
acquisition spend is in `acquisition.fetch`, not here.
domains.summary: Traces, spans, and normalized runtime events, month-partitioned (machinery lens).
domains.title: Observability

domains.body:
`orchestration.operation_intent` records intent_type (including knowledge_ingestion),
schema_version, payload, preconditions, unique `idempotency_key`, optional mission and
attempt, and approval_state. `orchestration.operation_receipt` is one-to-one with an
intent and immutable: outcome applied, rejected, noop, or partial, plus
changes_summary and affected_refs. Facts cannot exist without a receipt id.

`orchestration.artifact` is content-addressed (sha256, bucket_class, storage_bucket,
unique object_path) and typed by `orchestration.artifact_type`. Lineage
(`orchestration.artifact_lineage`) records derived_from, supersedes, corrects,
produced_by, consumed_by. Authored-work assets and uploaded sources from the product
also register here (`authored_work_asset`, `uploaded_document`, `file_set_file`).

pipeline_agent can select intents and artifacts but not receipt rows. `q:receipts.for_intent`
therefore joins the intent to `temporal.knowledge_batch` on idempotency_key to expose
receipt_id and knowledge_seq. Missions, attempts, work items, and capabilities are
the durable envelope; this workspace does not create Mission Control spine objects.
Most of this schema is verification plumbing (`orchestration.verification_*`), hidden from
START_HERE and MAP as machinery.
domains.summary: Missions, intents, immutable receipts, and content-addressed artifacts (machinery lens).
domains.title: Orchestration ledger

domains.body:
`api.product_command(p_workspace_id, p_operation, p_idempotency_key, p_expected_head,
p_payload)` resolves the actor and client grant, computes the input digest, replays a prior
`authoring.command` with the same idempotency key (CONFLICT when the input differs) and
dispatches to `product.dispatch_command`, which falls through to
`product.dispatch_research_command` for Build 07 research operations. `api.product_read`
dispatches to `product.dispatch_read` then `product.dispatch_research_read`;
`api.product_worker` (service_role only) to `product.dispatch_worker`. Unknown operations
fail with `UNKNOWN_OPERATION`; other failures are `product.fail(code, detail)` exceptions
(NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT, VALIDATION, EXPOSURE_BLOCKED, LIMIT_EXCEEDED).

The generator parses these bodies into one page per operation (`ops/<operation>.md`:
dispatcher, how to call, relations the arm touches, helpers called) and lists them in
INDEX.md. Helpers: `product.require_role` / `product.role_in` (workspace roles),
`product.new_event` (authoring events), `product.register_artifact` (content-addressed
uploads), `product.insert_revision` / `product.exposure` (authoring), `product.finalize`
(assessment), `product.dataset_*` (datasets), `product.support_*` (inquiry support).

Trap: the page lists relations by scanning the arm text — joins inside helper functions are
attributed to the helper's own page, not the operation.
domains.summary: The product's command/read/worker dispatchers; every `when '<op>' then` arm has a page under ops/.
domains.title: Product operations (dispatchers and helpers)

domains.body:
Build 08 reduced `ranking` to three tables. `ranking.leaderboard` names a ranked view:
the cohort filter, the metric (a `temporal.stream_kind`) and the policy are data in
`definition`; the values come from `temporal.segment`, never from a metric table of their
own. `ranking.leaderboard_edition` freezes one publication (membership, `knowledge_seq`,
`cohort`); `ranking.leaderboard_entry` is a ranked row with `score`, `unit`,
`explanation` and the `source_segment_ids` that produced it.

`q:ranking.leaderboard` (`api.leaderboard(p_slug, p_limit)`) returns the latest published
edition for `app_reader`. For ad-hoc comparison use the L1 views directly:
`q:catalog.models` (min price, capabilities), `q:catalog.benchmark_scores` (benchmark facts).
Trap: treating an edition as current world facts — it is a snapshot at its knowledge head;
cite the segments in `source_segment_ids` when you quote a score.
domains.summary: A leaderboard is a named ranked view over fact segments; editions freeze membership at a knowledge head.
domains.title: Leaderboards

domains.body:
`catalog.relationship` is the only edge table. `kind` references
`taxonomy.relationship_kind`, which lists `from_kinds`, `to_kinds`, whether the edge is
temporal, and a `property_schema`. Trigger `relationship_kinds` rejects illegal endpoint
kinds (SQLSTATE 23514). Current edges have `k_to` null; the unique current key is
`(tenant, kind, from, to, qualifier, episode)`. The L1 views fold the common edges into
columns (developer, provider, speakers, repositories, techniques), so read a view before
walking edges by hand.

Temporal kinds (employed_by, offered_by, …) also need an active `relationship_active`
stream on the relationship subject. `api.relationships` and `api.current_relationships`
hide temporal edges that are not active at the requested world time. Non-temporal kinds
(`offered_as`, `version_of`, `has_code`, `presented_at`, `about`, `cites`) are current
whenever `k_to` is null. `api.related(entity, kind, direction, at)` returns just the ids.

Read with `q:entity.relationships` (direction both, outgoing, incoming) or
`q:relationships.current_by_kind`. Check `q:vocab.relationship_kind` before composing a
relationship.assert proposal. Properties must satisfy property_schema via
`temporal.payload_valid`. `version_of` additionally requires a matching pair
(product_version/product, ai_model_version/ai_model, library_release/library).

Facets and terms in `taxonomy` classify entities, guidance items or authored works through
`taxonomy.assignment` (cardinality and target scope enforced by triggers); they are not
substitutes for relationship kinds. Agents never insert edges; `temporal.assert_relationship`
runs as `executor_service` inside a batch.
domains.summary: One relationship table; kinds constrain endpoints and may carry a relationship_active stream.
domains.title: Relationships and taxonomy

domains.body:
Build 08 collapsed retrieval into one stack. `retrieval.vector_item` is the searchable
item: `search_text`, `lens` (corpus | ours | private | evidence), `source_tier` (T0 verified
assertions, T1 our content, T2 primary corpus, T3 third-party, T4 live web — a filter and a
mild boost, never a truth claim), and facets `document_type_code`, `unit_kind`,
`entity_id`, `document_id`, `source_role_code`, `valid_during`, `knowledge_seq`,
`assurance_rank`, `start_ms`/`end_ms`, `workspace_id` for private items. Embeddings live in
`retrieval.vector_item_embedding_1536` partitions.

`retrieval.projection_target` says what an item is about — exactly one of entity card,
guidance item (`record_id`), chunk, claim, summary, typed unit (`document_node_id`), digest,
one of our authored revisions, or a private passage. `retrieval.index_text_item` is the one
way a text becomes searchable (idempotent on identical text). Spaces (`retrieval.vector_space`
slugs units, digests, entity_cards, assertions, own_content, learner_notes, knowledge_text, …)
are facets, not separate engines; publication (`retrieval.space_publication`) still gates
what `app_reader` may read.

`q:retrieval.search_unified` (`api.search_unified`) is L3: resolve the scope first (lenses,
tiers, space slugs, document types, unit kinds, entity ids, as-of, workspace ids for
private), then fuse english full-text, trigram and ANN (when the executor supplies an
embedding) with RRF. Private items are returned only for the workspaces passed in; the
product `search` operation passes the caller's workspaces. `q:retrieval.hybrid_search` is
the older per-space-version entry (needs an embedding, `execute: false`).

Packets (`retrieval.evidence_packet`, `retrieval.packet_member`) assemble verified claims,
guidance items and source-faithful representations with scores and locators for one
question; `q:retrieval.evidence_packet` returns one with node timecodes. Agents never write
embeddings; projection rebuilds are governed runtime operations. Trap: expecting
`search_unified` to embed the query in-database — without an embedding it is lexical only.
domains.summary: One retrieval stack: every searchable text is a vector item with lens, source tier and facets; api.search_unified scopes then fuses.
domains.title: Retrieval (one stack, lens and tier)

domains.body:
`staging.candidate` holds a proposed kind, payload, optional source, and optional
resolved entity. It is the identity-resolution zone. It is not a draft `temporal.segment`.
`staging.identity_match` records scored matches. `staging.resolution_decision`
(create, match, reject, defer) and `staging.vetting_decision` (admit, reject, defer)
each require a receipt.

`q:staging.unresolved` lists candidates with no create/match/reject decision.
`q:staging.candidates_for_kind` filters by `proposed_kind`. Low-confidence resolve
results should become candidate.stage (rule stage.when_confidence_below_threshold)
instead of entity.create.

`proposed_kind` must exist in `taxonomy.entity_kind`. Pipeline agents may insert
candidates; only the executor writes decisions with a receipt. Review tasks in
`evaluation` can point at a candidate. Do not park an uncertain price here — use belief
disputed or stage only the unknown organization. The source_id on the candidate should
point at the `evidence.source` that mentioned the name, so later merges have a quote.
domains.summary: Candidates for new identities, not a staging copy of facts.
domains.title: Staging and identity resolution

domains.body:
A fact is a `temporal.segment` on a `temporal.stream`. The stream is
`(kind, subject_entity_id | subject_relationship_id, scope_key)`. The segment carries
world interval `valid_during` and knowledge interval `[k_from, k_to)`. Current means
`k_to is null`. "As the world was at T, as we knew at K" is `q:entity.at`; the L1 tables
replayed at T are `q:catalog.models_at` and `q:catalog.model_offerings_at`.

Build 08 makes `temporal` the one home for numbers: `offering_price` (payload meter|tier|region,
amount+currency+unit), `benchmark_score`, `model_context_window`, `repository_stars`,
`organization_headcount`, `package_downloads` and so on are streams; `ranking` and the
L1 views only read them. `q:facts.price_history` shows every price belief of an offering
and meter with both clocks; `q:facts.changes_since` lists what changed since a date as
facts opened/replaced (with the old value), events and unit-level document diffs, with
`learned_at` (knowledge clock) beside `world_from` (world clock).

`temporal.knowledge_head` is one row per tenant. `q:knowledge.head` reads it as
`app_reader`. Writes open a batch with `temporal.begin_batch(p_expected_head)`; a mismatch
raises `rebase_required` (40001). `temporal.commit_batch` seals the batch against a receipt,
unique idempotency key and SHA-256 input digest, then validates stream slot rules (status,
amount, unit, currency, payload JSON Schema).

`temporal.assert_state` is a no-op when an identical current segment exists. Overlap closes
the old segment and re-inserts unaffected fragments with `replaces_segment_id`. Two
overlapping assertions in one batch are an error. `temporal_basis` explicit or
carry_forward requires a `temporal.extent`. Events are `temporal.event` plus a current
`temporal.event_occurrence`.

Traps: `api.current_facts` hides intervals that do not contain now() — use `q:entity.at`
for history and `q:entity.timeline` for unknown gaps. A new price series defaults its
scope_key to meter|tier|region; an existing series keeps its own scope_key, so read
`q:facts.price_history` before asserting a correction. Agents never DML temporal tables;
they submit fact.assert_state / event.assert intents.
domains.summary: A fact is a segment on a stream with a world interval and a knowledge interval; one home for every number.
domains.title: Temporal facts (two clocks)

rules.detail:
The alias unique key is per entity, not global. The same alias string may exist on two
entities. The executor rejects an alias that `api.resolve_entity` matches to a different
active canonical entity at score ≥ 0.98, so agents do not silently attach a well-known
name to the wrong id.
rules.title: Alias must not collide with another canonical entity

rules.detail:
`temporal.stream_kind:model_offering_availability` admits statuses announced, preview,
ga, deprecated, retired. The database does not order them. Hold a proposal that would
move a current status backward along that sequence unless the evidence is an explicit
correction with `temporal_basis=explicit` and a replacing interval. The same order
applies to `temporal.stream_kind:product_feature_availability` (removed instead of retired).
rules.title: Availability transitions are ordered

rules.detail:
`catalog.entity.kind` references `taxonomy.entity_kind(code)`. A `new` subject whose kind
is not a vocabulary code is rejected before a batch opens (`VOCABULARY_VIOLATION`).
Kind-specific attributes go into `catalog.entity.attributes` and are validated by trigger
`catalog.validate_entity_attributes` against `taxonomy.entity_kind.attributes_schema`
(for example `model_offering` requires `offering_key`, `ai_model_version` requires
`version_label`). Numbers that change over time are fact streams, never attributes.
rules.title: Entity kind must be in vocabulary and attributes must validate

rules.detail:
`temporal.segment.valid_during` is `not null` and `segment_valid_during_check` requires
a non-empty `[)` range bounded below. Events use the same shape on
`temporal.event_occurrence.occurred_during`. A proposal without `worldInterval.from`
is rejected.
rules.title: World-time required on facts

rules.detail:
`entity_identifier_scheme_check` restricts `scheme` to the closed list
(wikidata, ror, orcid, github, huggingface, npm, pypi, crates, go_module, doi, arxiv,
openreview, mcp_registry, cve, ghsa, spdx, crunchbase, pitchbook, linkedin, x,
youtube_channel, youtube_playlist, youtube_video, spotify, apple_podcasts, domain,
sec_cik, lei, isin, other). `(scheme, value)` is unique per tenant.
rules.title: Identifier namespace must be in vocabulary

rules.detail:
`temporal.commit_batch` requires `currency ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$'` for
`offering_price`, `compute_offering_price`, and `valuation`. Amount and a
unit from `unit_values` are also required (`requires_amount`).
rules.title: Monetary streams require ISO-4217 currency

rules.detail:
Two `offering_price` facts on the same subject and world interval do not collide only when
`scope_key` distinguishes them, so a **new** series with no `scopeKey` is rewritten to
`meter|tier|region` from the payload (for example `input_tokens||`); the exclusion
constraint `segment_stream_id_valid_during_excl` would otherwise reject the second
current segment. The database does not enforce any naming convention for `scope_key`:
a series that already exists for the same subject, stream and meter keeps whatever
`scope_key` it was created with. Read `q:facts.price_history` first; if a current segment
with the same meter exists under another `scope_key`, name that key explicitly, or the
stale segment stays current beside your new one. The payload `meter` is required by the
`temporal.stream_kind:offering_price` payload schema.
rules.title: A price series is keyed by meter (and tier, region); an existing series keeps its key

rules.detail:
`temporal.assert_state` returns the existing segment id when an identical current
segment exists. `temporal.knowledge_batch` is unique on `(tenant_id, idempotency_key)`
(`knowledge_batch_tenant_id_idempotency_key_key`). A second submit of the same intent
bytes returns `duplicate_of` without opening a new batch.
rules.title: Repeated identical proposals are no-ops

rules.detail:
Trigger `relationship_kinds` on `catalog.relationship` runs
`catalog.check_relationship_kinds` and raises if the from/to entity kinds are not in
`taxonomy.relationship_kind.from_kinds` / `to_kinds`. `version_of` additionally requires
a matching pair (product_version/product, ai_model_version/ai_model, …); the parent kind
is also recorded on `taxonomy.entity_kind.parent_kind`.
rules.title: Relationship kinds constrain entity kinds

rules.detail:
Closing a current segment (`k_to` set) without asserting a successor that starts at or
after the close instant leaves a world-time hole. `api.entity_timeline` will emit
`unknown` gaps. Reject a close-only proposal that does not supply a later
`worldInterval.from`. `temporal.close_segment` only stamps knowledge time; it does not
invent a replacement fact.
rules.title: Do not close a segment without a later world-time

rules.detail:
If `api.resolve_entity` or an identifier lookup scores below the configured threshold
(default 0.98 on identifier, lower on alias), rewrite entity.create to
candidate.stage with reason `identity_ambiguous` unless the intent says
`onMatch: use_existing`. `staging.candidate.proposed_kind` still must be a
`taxonomy.entity_kind` (`candidate_proposed_kind_fkey`).
rules.title: Stage when identity confidence is below threshold

rules.detail:
A fact may cite `primary_claim_id` only after the claim exists. The executor implies
claim.materialize for cited claims not yet in `evidence.claim`, then admits
support.admit through `temporal.admit_support`. `segment_support_claim_id_fkey` and
`segment_primary_claim_id_fkey` enforce the FK once rows exist; the ordering is an
executor rule so agents get a readable plan instead of a mid-batch FK failure.
rules.title: Support must precede claim materialization of a fact

rules.detail:
A fact read from a document unit (`content.document_node`) must name the
`content.unit_assertion_mapping` that interprets the unit kind into a stream, relationship
or event. Deterministic mappings on first-party structured units (`content.unit_kind:price_row`
on a `content.document_type:pricing_page`) take the cheap path; other mappings carry a
`risk_floor` and are held for Knowledge Services verification. The locator of the fact is the
unit's position, so `api.fact_locators` can show the exact row later.
rules.title: Typed units become assertions only through a declared mapping

rules.detail:
`temporal.begin_batch(p_expected_head)` locks `temporal.knowledge_head` and raises
`rebase_required` (SQLSTATE 40001) when `p_expected_head` is not null and does not
equal the current `knowledge_seq`. The ingestion executor always passes the snapshot
head. A write without `expectedKnowledgeHead` is rejected at plan time so a stale
snapshot cannot silently land.
rules.title: expected_head required for writes

entries.name: acquisition.fetches_for_url
entries.sql:
select f.id, f.origin_kind, f.origin_label, f.tool, f.tool_version, f.request_url, f.final_url,
       f.requested_at, f.completed_at, f.http_status, f.outcome, f.content_sha256, f.media_type,
       f.size_bytes, f.credits_used, f.cost_usd, f.failure_class, f.prior_capture_id
from acquisition.fetch f
where f.tenant_id = util.current_tenant_id()
  and ($1::text is null or f.request_url = $1 or f.final_url = $1)
order by f.requested_at desc, f.id
limit least(greatest(coalesce($2, 50), 1), 200)
entries.summary: Fetch ledger rows for a URL (who fetched, with what tool, outcome, hash, spend)

rel:catalog.entity.notes:
Build 08 dropped the thirty-six thin typed tables (corpus.organization, corpus.person,
corpus.ai_model, corpus.ai_model_version, corpus.model_offering, …). What they carried now
lives in `attributes`, validated per kind by `catalog.validate_entity_attributes`:
organization → legal_name, org_kind (frontier_lab, model_provider, cloud, tooling_vendor,
startup, enterprise, academic, nonprofit, media, event_organizer, investor, other),
website_url, country_code, founded_on; person → given_name, family_name, title,
affiliation_text, orcid, profile_url (also store scheme orcid on entity_identifier);
ai_model → model_family, modalities, description; ai_model_version (parent ai_model) →
version_label (required), provider_model_id, modalities, open_weights, model_page_url;
model_offering (parent ai_model_version) → offering_key (required; the provider-side SKU
or API model id), region, tier, pricing_url, provider_model_id; library → ecosystem,
package_name, repository_url, docs_url, category; paper → arxiv_id, doi, published_on,
venue; talk → talk_kind, track, level, session_id, video_url, slides_url, edition.
Anything that changes over time (price, context window, stars, headcount, availability)
is a fact stream, never an attribute. Work kinds also have a `catalog.work` row.
rel:catalog.entity.summary: One row per canonical identity; kind-specific attributes are a jsonb validated by taxonomy.entity_kind.attributes_schema.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "knowledge-ingestion-intent.v1",
  "intentId": "admit-price-support",
  "expectedKnowledgeHead": 41,
  "evidence": { "verificationRuns": [{ "runId": "vr_01J8Q000", "manifestDigest": "sha256:c0d0" }] },
  "subjects": [{ "ref": "offering", "mode": "resolved", "entityId": "0192b000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001", "kind": "model_offering" }],
  "proposals": [
    {
      "proposalId": "p-support",
      "kind": "support.admit",
      "targetRef": "0192b9aa-0000-7000-8000-000000000001",
      "supportRole": "primary",
      "belief": "accepted",
      "evidence": [{ "runId": "vr_01J8Q000", "claimId": "c_0011", "locatorRef": "q_06", "role": "primary" }]
    }
  ]
}
```
tasks.pitfalls: The claim must exist (materialize first). Locator is required. Role on the table is supports, challenges, or context — the intent `supportRole` primary/corroborating/contradicting is mapped by the executor. Support is written only through `temporal.admit_support`. A verified claim needs an admitted use decision (`verification.use_admission`).

tasks.expected_shape: A short list ordered by `input_usd_per_1m` with the offering, provider, region/tier, the capability status that qualified it and the benchmark row (`score`, `setting`, `claim_id`) that met the floor. Cite `price_locator_id` and `as_of_knowledge_seq`.
tasks.operation:
Filter first, then price, then verify the floor; a leaderboard edition can replace all three when one exists.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "knowledge-read-intent.v1",
  "intentId": "cheapest-with-tool-use",
  "operations": [
    { "opId": "models", "kind": "named_query", "query": "catalog.models", "params": { "text": null, "availability": "ga", "limit": 200 } },
    { "opId": "offers", "kind": "named_query", "query": "catalog.model_offerings", "params": { "model_version_id": null, "text": null, "limit": 200 } },
    { "opId": "scores", "kind": "named_query", "query": "catalog.benchmark_scores", "params": { "subject_id": null, "benchmark": "SWE-bench", "limit": 200 } },
    { "opId": "board", "kind": "named_query", "query": "ranking.leaderboard", "params": { "slug": "cheapest-frontier-input", "limit": 20 } }
  ]
}
```

Keep `models` rows where `tool_use = 'supported'` (or the status you need), join `offers` on `model_version_id` and take the lowest `input_usd_per_1m` whose subject has a `scores` row above the floor.
tasks.pitfalls: Cheapest input is not cheapest overall: weigh `output_usd_per_1m` and cached/batch meters by your traffic. Capability statuses are per model version; offerings of the same version share them. A missing benchmark row means unknown, not failed. Leaderboard editions are snapshots at a knowledge head; recompute from L1 when the head has moved.
tasks.title: Cheapest model that satisfies a capability or benchmark floor

tasks.expected_shape: One row: `knowledge_seq` (0 when no batch has been sealed), `updated_at`.
tasks.pitfalls: Freshness is the integer head, not executed_at. Two open writers cannot share a batch; the second sees knowledge batch already open. Always pass expectedKnowledgeHead (rule write.expected_head_required). Product operations use a different head: `p_expected_head` is the work's head revision id.
tasks.title: Check the knowledge head before writing

tasks.expected_shape: `models` rows: one per model version with `developer`, `released_on`, `context_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `modalities`, capability statuses (`tool_use`, `structured_output`, `reasoning`, `vision`), `knowledge_cutoff`, `availability`, `min_input_usd_per_1m`, `min_output_usd_per_1m`, `offering_count`, `as_of_knowledge_seq`. `scores` rows carry `score`, `unit`, `setting`, `claim_id`. A leaderboard row carries `source_segment_ids` in `explanation`.
tasks.navigation: `START_HERE.md` (L1) → `relations/api/models.md` → `q:catalog.models`; numbers you quote go back to `q:catalog.benchmark_scores` / `q:facts.locators`.
tasks.pitfalls: `api.models` shows the minimum current price across offerings; the offering that has it is in `q:catalog.model_offerings` (`model_version_id`). Capability columns are statuses of fact streams, not booleans from a spec sheet; `null` means no fact, not "no". Cite `as_of_knowledge_seq` with every table you paste. Do not rank by benchmark without the `setting` column — two scores with different settings are not comparable.

tasks.pitfalls: Every `fact.assert_state` that may correct an existing fact must carry the `scopeKey` of the series it corrects (run `tasks/find-stale-facts.md` first). `streamKind`, `relationshipKind`, `eventKind`, and subject `kind` are vocabulary codes (`vocab.*` queries); a wrong code is `VOCABULARY_VIOLATION` before any transaction; subject `attributes` must satisfy the kind's schema. `expectedKnowledgeHead` comes from the read snapshot; a moved head is `REBASE_REQUIRED` unless `onStale` allows a disjoint rebase. Submit an intent once; the same `intentId` again returns `duplicateOf`. `claim.materialize` needs `context.attemptId`.

Every stale slot you find becomes one `fact.assert_state` proposal on the **same** `streamKind` and `scopeKey` (see `tasks/supersede-stale-fact.md`); the snapshot head is your `expectedKnowledgeHead`. `diffs` rows with `change_kind = attribute_changed` on a `price_row` are the refresh pipeline's own stale candidates (`update_proposal_state`).

tasks.operation:
Read the current segments per stream and compare each `(stream_kind, scope_key)` slot with what the source states. A fact is stale when the slot exists, its segment is current (`k_to` null), and the source gives a different value with a later world time.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "knowledge-read-intent.v1",
  "intentId": "stale-scan-codex",
  "operations": [
    { "opId": "resolve", "kind": "named_query", "query": "entity.resolve", "params": { "text": "Codex" } },
    { "opId": "prices", "kind": "named_query", "query": "facts.current_by_stream", "params": { "stream_kind": "offering_price", "entity_id": "$resolve.rows[0].entity_id", "limit": 100 } },
    { "opId": "history", "kind": "named_query", "query": "facts.price_history", "params": { "offering_id": "$resolve.rows[0].entity_id", "meter": "input_tokens" } },
    { "opId": "diffs", "kind": "named_query", "query": "content.unit_changes", "params": { "document_id": null, "since": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", "limit": 100 } },
    { "opId": "head", "kind": "named_query", "query": "knowledge.head" }
  ]
}
```
tasks.pitfalls: Writing the new value under a new `scopeKey` does not fix anything: the old segment stays current and the entity now has two contradicting current facts. Reuse the existing slot's `scope_key` exactly. Facts without a world time in the source are not corrections; record them with `temporalBasis: unresolved` or stage them.
tasks.title: Find facts the database still holds as current that a source contradicts

tasks.expected_shape: Rows: `work_id`, `work_kind`, `work_slug`, `revision_id`, `revision_title`, `revision_created_at`, `software`, `release`, `released_at`, `breaking`, `binding` (uses | covers | requires), `version_spec`. `breaking = true` rows need review first.
tasks.pitfalls: Only head revisions authored *before* the release appear; a revision created after it is assumed to know about it. `version_spec` is the author's declared range — a release inside the range is not "affected" unless `breaking`. terminology.definition: Executor decision that a proposal becomes a canonical fact through the temporal helpers. A verified claim's receipt must name an admitted use decision, recorded in verification.use_admission by verification.assert_admitted_use in the same transaction. Distinct from receipt outcome applied and from plan outcomes such as review_required or held.

A typed alternate name (synonym, acronym, former_name, handle, ticker, slug, misspelling, translation, model_alias). Unique per (entity, normalized alias, alias_kind), not globally unique across entities.
Content-addressed stored object (sha256, bucket_class, storage_bucket, object_path) typed by artifact_type. Lineage edges record derived_from, supersedes, corrects, produced_by, consumed_by.

content.unit_assertion_mapping declares how a unit kind's attributes become an assertion (a stream kind, relationship, event or attribute) with subject, value, qualifier and time templates. Deterministic mappings on first-party structured units take the cheap path; others carry a risk floor and go through Knowledge Services verification. evidence.extraction_record records which mapping interpreted which unit.
How strongly a guidance item or vector item is backed. guidance.assurance_level is the vocabulary; retrieval filters accept a minimum assurance rank.
accepted, disputed, or unknown on a segment or occurrence. disputed does not replace an accepted current segment; the executor plans review_required.

One row in catalog.entity. kind picks the taxonomy.entity_kind whose attributes_schema validates the row's attributes jsonb. lifecycle is active, merged, or retired. Numbers that change over time are fact streams, never attributes.

content.structure_census records what a captured representation structurally contains (headings, tables, lists, code, timecodes, speakers, figures, machine blocks) before any document kind or grammar is assigned. Kinds are open-world: a document_type can be candidate until its grammar settles, and promotion candidates come from census statistics.
An atomic statement with claim_type, status, and created_by_receipt_id. Facts may cite a claim as primary_claim_id. Subjects are attached via claim_subject roles subject, object, or context.
Catalog hint for statement_timeout and EXPLAIN gates. cheap and medium default to 15s; heavy is 60s and must not sequential-scan large relations.

content.document_digest is a structured digest of a document version (or a section/entity view) whose content.digest_item rows are records anchored to unit node ids — key points, entity roles, assertion references, changes, open questions, limitations, research directions. Prose summaries in content.document_summary render a digest; prose without a digest is not evidence.
A curated map of 5–20 relations that belong together (identity, temporal-facts, content, …). Default domain for a schema is schema_domains; a relation overlay may override it.

taxonomy.entity_kind.code. Carries attributes_schema (validates catalog.entity.attributes), parent_kind (model version -> model; the link itself is a catalog.relationship) and is_work. catalog.entity.kind is a foreign key; unknown kinds cannot be inserted.
A retrieval-assembled bundle of members (verified claims, guidance items, source-faithful representations with scores and locators) for one question. Read with api.evidence_packet.
Source text for a date with precision (instant, day, month, quarter, year, relative, unknown) and optional earliest/latest bounds. Required when temporal_basis is explicit or carry_forward.

acquisition.fetch is one attempt to obtain bytes from a URL — who (origin), with what tool, outcome, hash, spend — recorded before it becomes an evidence.source_capture. outcome unchanged means the same bytes as prior_capture_id, so no new document version; content.refresh_check records that per document.
Digest of schema structure plus vocabularies, or of workspace plus enrichment. Artifacts also carry content sha256. Ingestion intents cite workspaceFingerprint; mismatch is WORKSPACE_STALE.

guidance.item is one expert knowledge statement typed by guidance.item_kind (technical_problem, solution_pattern, failure_mode, compatibility_constraint, operational_practice, implementation_example, security_consideration, advanced_usage_pattern, setup_guide_step, research_direction) with a payload validated by that kind's schema, an assurance level, a provenance claim and the entities it is about (guidance.item_subject). Created only under a receipt.

authoring.work.head_revision_id, the current immutable authoring.work_revision of a course, module, lesson, activity, brief, report or dataset. Commands that change a work pass p_expected_head; a stale head is CONFLICT. api.works_authored lists works at their head.

api.search_unified fuses english full-text, trigram and (when an embedding is given) ANN channels with reciprocal rank fusion over the one stack, filtered by lens, tier, space, document kind, unit kind, entity, as-of and workspace. api.hybrid_knowledge_search_1536 is the older per-space-version entry.

Unique per tenant on operation_intent, knowledge_batch and authoring.command (product operations). A second submit of the same bytes returns the existing receipt or result; the same key with different input is CONFLICT.
A schemed external identifier. scheme is a closed check-constraint vocabulary. Unique per tenant on (scheme, value), so one identifier names at most one entity.
A durable proposed operation. knowledge-read-intent.v1 and knowledge-ingestion-intent.v1 are the workspace contracts; the ledger row is orchestration.operation_intent with an idempotency_key.
One committed admission transaction. commit_batch writes a knowledge_batch row with a receipt, idempotency key, and input digest, then advances the tenant head by one.

The four answer levels every question routes through. L1 catalog tables (api.models, api.software, …) filter, compare and rank without embeddings; L2 facts and time (api.changes_since, api.price_history, api.fact_locators, api.entity_at) answer what was true when and where it was read; L3 scoped semantic search (api.search_unified, api.talk_segments, api.document_units, api.document_digest) finds passages inside a scope; L4 is a budgeted agent loop over L1–L3 that files its result as a report.
Per-tenant monotonic sequence of sealed knowledge batches. Every snapshot and ingestion intent cites it; begin_batch fails rebase_required when the expected head does not match.
When a fact was admitted or closed. Stamped from the open batch. Current rows have k_to null; closed rows keep history. api.changes_since reports learned_at beside world_from.

Whose knowledge a row is. corpus is ingested industry knowledge (catalog, content, temporal, taxonomy, staging, acquisition, ranking, guidance, retrieval, the api catalog views); ours is what we author and learn (authoring, learning, access, library, inquiry, dataset, product, api.works_authored); private is one workspace's passages and conversations (RLS-isolated); evidence is claims, locators and admissions; machinery and legacy are runtime plumbing hidden from START_HERE and MAP. Every search-index entry and page carries a lens; retrieval.vector_item.lens and api.search_unified p_lenses use the same words.

A precise selection inside a capture (text_quote, table cell, media_timecode, page+bbox, JSON pointer, line range) with selected_content_sha256 and a normalized value. Support rows require a locator; api.fact_locators shows the locator, capture and typed unit behind a current fact.

unit_kind plus the values of the kind's logical_key_attributes (for a price_row offering|meter|tier|region), so the same unit can be matched across versions of a document. content.unit_change diffs versions by logical key; api.changes_since reports those diffs beside fact changes.

The thing an offering price is charged per (input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, batch_input_tokens, …). Required in the offering_price payload; with tier and region it forms the price series scope_key, and api.price_history takes it as p_meter.

orchestration.mission is the durable work envelope. Intents, artifacts and acquisition.fetch rows may record mission ids. Mission Control admission is out of band; this workspace only stores the id when supplied.
An entry in the knowledge-query-catalog. Agents pass a name and params; they never send SQL. Build validation executes each example under the catalog role.

One `when '<op>' then` arm of product.dispatch_command / dispatch_read / dispatch_worker / dispatch_research_*, called through api.product_command(workspace, op, idempotency_key, expected_head, payload), api.product_read or api.product_worker. Each has a page under ops/ listing the relations the arm touches.

A derived retrieval object (search_projection, vector_item) pointing at a projection_target (entity card, guidance item, chunk, claim, summary, typed unit, digest, our authored revision or a private passage). retrieval.index_text_item is the one way a text becomes searchable; agents never write embeddings.
A published vector-space version that search is allowed to read. Unpublished or inactive versions raise insufficient_privilege.
Transaction failure (SQLSTATE 40001) from begin_batch when expected head does not match the locked knowledge_head. Not a per-proposal outcome.
Immutable orchestration.operation_receipt for one intent. Outcome is applied, rejected, noop, or partial. Facts and entities require a receipt id before they can be written.
taxonomy.relationship_kind.code with from_kinds, to_kinds, temporal flag, and property_schema. Trigger catalog.check_relationship_kinds rejects illegal endpoints.

Two meanings. authoring.release freezes a root revision's closure for distribution (freeze_release, offer_release); a software release in the corpus is a library_release entity whose release_published event and version facts api.software_releases lists, and api.modules_affected_by_release connects the two.

Enabled on tenant tables. Typical policy km_tenant_access uses tenant_id = util.current_tenant_id(). Private-lens rows (library.passage, conversation.*) are additionally isolated per workspace; api.search_unified returns them only for the workspaces passed in.

NOLOGIN Postgres roles. app_reader sees api views and RPCs. pipeline_agent selects bounded schemas. executor_service alone executes temporal helpers and writes catalog facts. Product operations run as authenticated (api.product_command / api.product_read) or service_role (api.product_worker).

Distinguishes parallel series on the same subject and stream kind (meter|tier|region for prices, episode for engagements). Default is the empty string. Part of the stream unique key; the database enforces no naming convention, so a correction must reuse the existing series key.
One assertion of a fact on a stream. Carries a world interval valid_during and a knowledge interval [k_from, k_to). Current means k_to is null.

A filter and a mild ranking boost, never a truth claim. T0 verified assertions, T1 our own content, T2 primary corpus (first party about itself, filers, registries), T3 third-party corpus, T4 live web. content.source_role.default_source_tier seeds it from who speaks; retrieval.vector_item.source_tier carries it; api.search_unified p_tiers filters on it.
An unresolved proposed identity. Not a staging copy of a fact. Resolution decisions are create, match, reject, or defer; vetting decisions are admit, reject, or defer.
The identity of a fact series, unique on (kind, subject entity or relationship, scope_key). Segments stack on a stream; overlapping current segments are forbidden.

temporal.stream_kind.code with subject_mode, subject_kinds, status_values, unit_values, requires_amount, and payload_schema. commit_batch validates slot rules. offering_price is the one home for prices (payload meter|tier|region), benchmark_score the one home for benchmark numbers.
A k-stamped link from a claim and locator to a segment or event occurrence. Written only through temporal.admit_support inside an open batch.

A question family with navigation, a read or ingestion operation, expected shape, and pitfalls. The shortest path from a natural-language question to a valid catalog query, product operation or intent.
Why the world interval is believed. explicit and carry_forward require an extent; observation_bounded is “true at capture time”; unresolved is an admitted gap.
Isolation key read from GUC app.tenant_id by util.current_tenant_id(). Missing context fails closed. RLS policies compare tenant_id to that function.
World time and knowledge time together. entity.at(entity, T, K) answers what was true at T as we knew it at K; price_history shows every belief with both clocks.

A content.document_node with a unit_kind from the content.unit_kind grammar (price_row, transcript_segment, release_entry, table_row, slide, section, …), attributes validated by that kind's JSON Schema, a logical_key stable across captures and a typed position (offsets, page, bbox, timecodes). Units are the anchors for locators, entity roles, extraction records and retrieval items; chunks are derived from units, never the other way round.

A named retrieval space (units, digests, entity_cards, assertions, own_content, learner_notes, knowledge_text, …) with versions and publications. api.search_unified takes space slugs as a facet; agents read only published versions.

A knowledge_verification component run that must be sealed before cited claims may be materialized; the database records the admitted use in verification.use_admission and a verified claim names an admission-bound receipt.

Allowlisted code tables such as taxonomy.entity_kind, taxonomy.relationship_kind, temporal.stream_kind, content.document_type, content.unit_kind, content.format, content.source_role and guidance.item_kind. Slot rules and endpoint kinds are enforced at write time.

catalog.work is the bibliographic row behind an entity whose kind is a work (paper, talk, media work, story, case study; taxonomy.entity_kind.is_work). Its content lives in content.document rows that point back through work_entity_id.

Generated projection of schema-ir.v1 into Markdown layers, search indexes, operation pages and the named-query catalog. Agents search then read a domain or task page; they never read schema-ir.json whole. Not to be confused with authoring.workspace, the product's team container.
When the world was like this. Stored as a tstzrange bounded below with [) bounds. Distinct from when we came to know it.
